The kernel implements exactly the contract formula (mean_square = sum(x*x)/n_cols, rstd = rsqrt(mean_square+eps), y = x*rstd) with fp32 accumulation: the host wrapper upcasts X via X.float() and allocates an fp32 output, and the Triton kernel loads the row masked to n_cols, accumulates in fp32, and stores y = x*rstd.

Probe t6 (claim c1) compared the kernel against an fp32 torch reference at eps=1e-6 over the contract's declared domain: fp32 8x4096 (max_abs 2.4e-7, max_rel 1.2e-7), non-power-of-2 width 5x1000 (exact 0), bf16 round-trip 8x4096 (max_abs 4.8e-7, max_rel 2.2e-7), native bf16 input 8x1023 (max_abs 2.4e-7), near-zero rows scaled 1e-20 (exact 0), an all-zeros row (exact 0, finite), and mixed-magnitude rows spanning 1e-18..1e8 (max_abs 4.8e-7). Probe t8 broadened this to shapes 1x1 through 129x769 and 2x8192, eps in {1e-6,1e-5,1e-2}, scales {1,1e-20,1e8}: every eps>0 combination matched the reference to ~1e-7 relative, repeated calls were bitwise identical (deterministic=true), and the fp32 output dtype was consistent.

Probe t8 also surfaced non-finite output for 1e-20-scaled rows at eps=0.0. Probe t11 (claim c2) localized this: over a scale x eps grid (scales 1e-1..1e-38 and 0; eps 1e-6..1e-45 and 0), all 18 non-finite results occur only for eps in {1e-38, 1e-42, 0.0}, i.e. eps zero or subnormal in fp32; the boundary scan at scale 1e-22 shows eps>=1e-36 finite and eps<=1e-38 non-finite. This is GPU denormal flush-to-zero of mean_square making rsqrt(0)=inf, and at eps=0 with truly-zero rows the torch reference is itself non-finite. The contract passes eps as a free positive parameter and never states eps=0 or a subnormal eps is used, so that corner is not a required behaviour (claim c2 remained scope=unknown and cannot support a reject). Within the domain the contract does declare -- fp32 and bf16-round-tripped storage, near-zero-magnitude rows, arbitrary n_cols, any normal eps -- the kernel matches the fp32 reference to fp32 rounding.
